lessons.name: THE GREYS ARE THE DIAGONAL: red, green and blue equal gives 256 colours out of 16777216 — one in 65536, which is 2^16. Two of the three channels carry no information on that diagonal, and the line proves the ratio rather than describing it.
lessons.why: THE GREYS ARE THE DIAGONAL: red, green and blue equal gives 256 colours out of 16777216 — one in 65536, which is 2^16. Two of the three channels carry no information on that diagonal, and the line proves the ratio rather than describing it.

lessons.name: A COLOUR IS SIX HEX CHARACTERS: #RRGGBB at four bits each is 24 bits, and 16^6 equals 2^24 exactly — the hexadecimal reading and the binary reading are one number, 16777216 colours.
lessons.why: A COLOUR IS SIX HEX CHARACTERS: #RRGGBB at four bits each is 24 bits, and 16^6 equals 2^24 exactly — the hexadecimal reading and the binary reading are one number, 16777216 colours.

lessons.name: THE THREE-DIGIT SHORTHAND #RGB EXPANDS EACH CHARACTER TWICE, so it reaches 16^3 = 4096 colours — one in 4096 of the full space. A palette written in shorthand is not a small notation for all colours; it is a notation for a sixteen-thousandth of them.
lessons.why: THE THREE-DIGIT SHORTHAND #RGB EXPANDS EACH CHARACTER TWICE, so it reaches 16^3 = 4096 colours — one in 4096 of the full space. A palette written in shorthand is not a small notation for all colours; it is a notation for a sixteen-thousandth of them.

lessons.name: EACH CHANNEL IS TWO HEXBITS — one byte, 256 levels — and three channels of eight bits close the twenty-four. The colour is not a number that prints in hex; it is three bytes, and the hex is how a byte is spelled.
lessons.why: EACH CHANNEL IS TWO HEXBITS — one byte, 256 levels — and three channels of eight bits close the twenty-four. The colour is not a number that prints in hex; it is three bytes, and the hex is how a byte is spelled.

lessons.name: THE DIVISORS THE WHEEL ADMITS below twenty are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 15, 18, 20 — nine and six among them, sixteen not. Forty degrees is the ninefold step the aura already walks, sixty the sextant of primaries and secondaries.
lessons.why: THE DIVISORS THE WHEEL ADMITS below twenty are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 15, 18, 20 — nine and six among them, sixteen not. Forty degrees is the ninefold step the aura already walks, sixty the sextant of primaries and secondaries.

lessons.name: THE HUE WHEEL DOES NOT DIVIDE BY SIXTEEN: 16 x 22 = 352 and 16 x 23 = 368 straddle 360, so no whole-degree step cuts the circle into sixteen. It divides by NINE at forty degrees and by SIX at sixty — the storage is hexadecimal while the geometry is not, and the line proves the failure rather than leaving it implied. Every degree named here is the whole-turn convention divided by an integer, not a quantity anyone observed.
